land.text: the province of Judaea and Galilee, cleared of Roman authority after Gallus's defeat

predecessors.note: The roman-empire dossier carries the matching contest 66-70 (counterpart 'Jewish rebels of Judaea').

land.text: Judaea, which 'later became a directly ruled province' (the roman-empire dossier's note)

successors.note: Herodium, Machaerus and Masada stayed in rebel hands after the fall of Jerusalem; Masada fell in 73/74.

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: A popular assembly 'convened at the Jerusalem Temple and established a provisional government'; Jerusalem fell in the summer of 70 (8 September 70, infobox of the siege page).

correction.text: the provisional government's military districts: 'Galilee and Gaulanitis, Jericho, Jaffa, Lydda, Emmaus, Thamna, Idumaea, Perea, Gophna, and Acrabetta' (only Judea, Galilee and Golan are drawn)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'After Gallus' defeat, a popular assembly convened at the Jerusalem Temple and established a provisional government' that 'divided the country into military districts' (First Jewish-Roman War page); Josephus was made commander of Galilee and Gaulanitis. Idumaea, Perea and the Samarian districts are listed but not drawn. The page gives no territorial summary or area.

correction.text: Judea, left to the rebels after Vespasian's conquest of Galilee and Gaulanitis in 67

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Vespasian's offensive on Galilee in 67 (Yodfat fell in June or July, Gamla in late October) takes Galilee and Gaulanitis; Judea is what remains. Drawn as the gazetteer's Judea region (9 thousand km2); the coast at Yavneh and Azotus was 'subdued and garrisoned' around the turn of 67/68.

correction.text: Jerusalem and its approaches: 'During the siege, the rebels held Jerusalem' (Siege of Jerusalem page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In spring 68, Vespasian systematically subdued settlements en route to Jerusalem' (First Jewish-Roman War page); 'During the siege, the rebels held Jerusalem' (13 April-8 September 70, Siege of Jerusalem page). The land between is not on either page; Jerusalem alone (40 km radius) is drawn. Herodium, Machaerus and Masada, held after 70, are single fortresses and are not drawn.

region.text: the provisional government's military districts: 'Galilee and Gaulanitis, Jericho, Jaffa, Lydda, Emmaus, Thamna, Idumaea, Perea, Gophna, and Acrabetta' (only Judea, Galilee and Golan are drawn)

ledger.note: 66: the Jewish provisional government is set up in Jerusalem. 'In May 66, violence erupted in the city of Caesarea'; 'After Gallus' defeat, a popular assembly convened at the Jerusalem Temple and established a provisional government' led by Ananus ben Ananus, Joseph ben Gurion and Joshua ben Gamla, which 'divided the country into military districts'. Gallus was routed after camping on Mount Scopus in late Tishrei (September-October); the page gives no month for the government.

region.text: Galilee and Gaulanitis, taken by Vespasian in 67

ledger.note: 67: Vespasian conquers Galilee. 'In early summer of 67, Vespasian established his base at Akko-Ptolemais before launching an offensive on Galilee'; Yodfat fell in June or July 67 and Gamla was taken 'in late October'. The page does not say Galilee and Gaulanitis were wholly lost by the end of 67; Josephus had been made commander of 'Galilee and Gaulanitis'.

region.text: the rest of Judea outside Jerusalem: 'In spring 68, Vespasian systematically subdued settlements en route to Jerusalem'

ledger.note: spring 68: Vespasian subdues the settlements on the road to Jerusalem. 'In spring 68, Vespasian systematically subdued settlements en route to Jerusalem'; around the turn of 67/68 Yavneh and Azotus were 'subdued and garrisoned'. The page names no place held by the rebels besides Jerusalem; winter 67/68 saw the Zealots consolidate control over Jerusalem 'through terror'.

region.text: Jerusalem and its approaches: 'During the siege, the rebels held Jerusalem' (Siege of Jerusalem page)

ledger.note: 8 September 70: Jerusalem falls. 'By early September, the conquest of Jerusalem was complete'; the siege ran '13 April - 8 September 70 CE' (infobox); the Temple was burned on the tenth of Av (late August) and the Upper City fell last, after the final assault of 7 Elul. First Jewish-Roman War page: 'fell in the summer of 70'. Herodium, Machaerus and Masada 'remained under rebel control until Roman forces took them later' (Masada 73/74).

wars.name: First Jewish-Roman War

zones.text: the provisional government's military districts: 'Galilee and Gaulanitis, Jericho, Jaffa, Lydda, Emmaus, Thamna, Idumaea, Perea, Gophna, and Acrabetta' (only Judea, Galilee and Golan are drawn)

wars.outcome: Roman victory: Vespasian's Galilee campaign in 67, the road to Jerusalem in 68, the siege of Jerusalem from 13 April to 8 September 70 and the Temple destroyed; Masada fell in 73/74.
wars.note: The page's infobox result line is cut off at 'Roman victory;'. Civil strife among the rebels: the Zealots' terror in winter 67/68, the Idumaeans in Jerusalem, John of Gischala and Simon bar Giora. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: war end cut from 74 to 70 to keep the war inside the state's life (dissolve at the fall of Jerusalem, September 70); the holdouts to Masada (73/74) belong to the roman-empire dossier's war.]

certainty.note: The districts are listed by name; no page gives a boundary.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, named by the roman-empire dossier ('Jewish rebels of Judaea', contest 66-70). Two pages opened. The pages give neither an extent nor an area; the keyframes follow the military districts named on the First Jewish-Roman War page and Vespasian's dated campaigns, and the 68-70 shape (Jerusalem alone) is a bridge. The Gallus date: the page gives late Tishrei (September-October) for Mount Scopus, not November. Wikidata id unknown. The 132-135 rebel state is bar-kokhba-state. Gazetteer: 'Idumaea' = Edom (not drawn), 'Perea' is not a region name.
